description: Palladium is a rare and lustrous silvery-white metal with chemical symbol Pd and atomic number 46. It was discovered in 1802 by English chemist William Hyde Wollaston and belongs to the platinum group metals. It is the least dense and has the lowest melting point of the platinum group metals.
uses: More than half the supply of palladium is used in catalytic converters, which convert harmful gases in automobile exhaust into nontoxic substances. Palladium is also used in electronics, dentistry, medicine, hydrogen purification, chemical applications, jewelry, and as catalysts in organic chemistry reactions.
characteristics: Palladium is a soft silver-white metal that is soft and ductile when annealed, becoming harder when cold-worked. It does not react with oxygen at standard temperature and thus does not tarnish in air. It dissolves slowly in concentrated nitric and sulfuric acids, readily in aqua regia at room temperature, and dissolves readily in aqua regia.
